profile.campus: Widows Creek, Jackson County, Alabama (former TVA Widows Creek Fossil Plant site near Bridgeport)
profile.address: County Road 459, Widows Creek Station, Jackson County, Alabama, 35740
profile.reading:
This building sits on the 360-acre former Widows Creek Fossil Plant site near Bridgeport, a coal-fired power plant the Tennessee Valley Authority operated for 63 years, employing more than 500 workers directly, before shutting it down in 2015 as part of TVA's broader coal retirement program. Google announced in April 2018 that it would build a roughly 600 million dollar data center on the site, its eighth US data center and fourteenth globally at the time, with TVA committing to supply the facility with renewable power sourced from solar, wind, or hydroelectric generation rather than the coal power the plant had produced for decades. Alabama and Jackson County officials framed the project as turning the economic loss of the coal plant's closure into new opportunity. Google contributed a 100,000 dollar grant to Jackson County schools for STEM programming around the time of the announcement, and the fully built-out complex was projected to support 75 to 100 permanent jobs. Construction of a dedicated solar farm to help power the campus began in 2019, according to Google's own Alabama location page.

Google has continued investing in the site well beyond the original announcement. By its own account the company has put more than 2 billion dollars into Alabama since building the Jackson County data center in 2018, and it credits its Alabama operations with generating about 2.6 billion dollars in economic activity in 2025. In 2026 Google said it would add a further 1.5 billion dollars to expand the campus through 2027, and agreed to cover the electricity its own operations consume plus infrastructure costs tied directly to the facility, a commitment TVA highlighted when it approved a 10 percent data center electricity rate increase phased in starting October 2026 to keep expansion costs from falling on other ratepayers. Google is also working with TVA and Kairos Power on a next generation power source for the site. TVA plans to purchase electricity from Kairos' Hermes 2 advanced nuclear demonstration project, with up to 50 megawatts earmarked to support Google's Alabama and Tennessee data centers once that project comes online.

Beyond the Jackson County campus itself, Google frames its Alabama presence as a broader economic development relationship with the state. The company says its Grow with Google workforce program has trained more than 153,000 Alabamians and that more than 17,000 small businesses across the state have received free training through Alabama Grow with Google coaches, and it reports more than 28 million dollars in philanthropic giving in Alabama since 2009. These are statewide figures rather than figures specific to this campus, but Google presents the Jackson County data center as the anchor investment that opened its broader Alabama relationship.

Google's data center locations page does not publish which of the two mapped Widows Creek buildings serves which function, nor their individual square footage or megawatt capacity, so this registry records the campus level investment and power figures as regional context rather than assigning them to this specific structure. This building is mapped at County Road 459 near the Widows Creek Station address, a short distance from a second Google building on the same parcel reached from County Road 96.

profile.research_note: Cowork facility-page writer 2026-09-06 pass: expanded reading using Google's own datacenters.google/locations/alabama page for verified Alabama investment (more than 2 billion dollars since 2018), a 2025 economic activity figure (2.6 billion dollars), a 2019 solar farm construction start date, and statewide Grow with Google (153,000+ trained) and philanthropic (28 million dollars+) figures, framed explicitly as Alabama-wide rather than facility-specific. Removed a semicolon to match house style. Added campus_power_note and campus_buildings_total (2) so both mapped Widows Creek buildings share identical campus-level facts, reflecting Google's continued non-disclosure of which building serves which function or their individual sqft/MW. This session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before this pass; a Jackson County Revenue Commissioner parcel lookup and TVA's own newsroom were attempted via direct fetch but were unreachable (DNS/robots failures), so building-level (as opposed to campus-level) specificity remains a genuine, documented gap rather than an oversight.
profile.regional_context: Google announced in 2026 that it would invest an additional $1.5 billion to expand the Jackson County campus through 2027, and agreed to cover the electricity its own operations consume plus infrastructure costs directly tied to the facility so expansion costs are not shifted onto TVA's other ratepayers, a commitment that came alongside TVA's approval of a 10% data center electricity rate increase phased in from October 2026.
profile.campus_power_note: Google and TVA have not published a combined power capacity figure for the Jackson County campus. TVA supplies the site with renewable power from solar, wind, or hydroelectric generation rather than the retired coal plant's generation, and TVA has said up to 50 megawatts from the Kairos Power Hermes 2 advanced nuclear demonstration project is earmarked, once operational, to support Google's combined Alabama and Tennessee data center load, not this campus alone. No campus-wide utility interconnection size, IT load, or standby generation figure has been made public by Google or TVA.

reading.body:
Google operates a data center in Bridgeport, Alabama, in Jackson County near the Tennessee River. The company publishes aggregate investment figures for its Alabama campuses but does not disclose the specific power capacity, square footage, or building count for individual facilities. The exact size and load of this campus therefore cannot be determined from published sources.

Alabama has twelve mapped data center facilities, of which only two publish power specifications totaling 9.5 MW of IT-relevant capacity. This Google campus is ranked third by published capacity in the state, though that ranking reflects the scarcity of disclosure rather than confirmed size. Most facilities in Alabama, like this one, release no technical specifications.

Without published power or facility data, the strategic relevance of this campus to AI scaling cannot be assessed from operator disclosures. Its location near the Tennessee River suggests potential access to hydroelectric generation, but grid constraints, cooling water availability, and actual committed load remain unknown. Determining its role in AI infrastructure requires either regulatory filings, utility records, or further operator transparency.
